Signed-off-by: Tong Zhigao <tongzhigao@pingcap.com>

<!-- Thank you for contributing to TiDB!

PR Title Format:
1. pkg [, pkg2, pkg3]: what's changed
2. *: what's changed

-->

### What problem does this PR solve?

Issue Number: close #14632 <!-- REMOVE this line if no issue to close -->

Problem Summary: 
- Distinct count very slow and might consume high amount of memory.
- If relative error is allowed, we can use sampling algorithm to compute approximate result.

### What is changed and how it works?

- Add new agg function `APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT`.

- Use `BJKST` algorithm to compute approximate result of distinct count. 

- For the calculation state, it uses a sample of element hash values with a size up to 2^16. Compared with the widely known HyperLogLog algorithm, this algorithm is less effective in terms of accuracy and memory consumption (even up to proportionality), but it is adaptive. This means that with fairly high accuracy, it consumes less memory during simultaneous computation of cardinality for a large number of data sets whose cardinality has power law distribution (i.e. in cases when most of the data sets are small). This algorithm is also very accurate for data sets with small cardinality and very efficient on CPU.

- It's better not to use this aggregation function if number of distinct element is bigger than 5 * 10^10.

- For TiFlash, TiDB can push down cop request and merge all partial result. For other engine, TiDB needs to collect all original data and compute all by itself.

Tests <!-- At least one of them must be included. -->

- Unit test

### Release note <!-- bugfixes or new feature need a release note -->
- Add new agg function `APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT` to support approximate count distinct.

issue_context.title: Implement approximate solution of distinct count
issue_context.body:
## Feature Request

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe:**
User found distinct count very slow and might consume high amount of memory.


**Describe the feature you'd like:**
SELECT HLL_DISTINCT_COUNT(A) from TBL;
Either TiKV Cop or TiFlash Cop compute hyperloglog of distinct key from each region and group. TiDB therefore merge the HLL result from each group. Essentially HLL provide a data structure that support add, count and merge. Results from each region cop / group can be merged together forms a final results. This final results has a bounded error margin.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HyperLogLog


**Describe alternatives you've considered:**
No.

**Teachability, Documentation, Adoption, Migration Strategy:**
A simple new function. Just need to tell user its not accurate but a lot faster.
comments: maybe we can utilize this package: https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/DataDog/hyperloglog?tab=doc
@zz-jason It better to use BJKST algorithm for lower error rate. According to http://www.vldb.org/pvldb/vol11/p499-harmouch.pdf. This algorithm is also default for clickhouse.

review_comments: Why CompleteMode and Partial1Mode share the same signature?

In case of partition table, `union` need to compute partial result to partial result.
We can detect and handle this case by checking whether return type is string.
Why we need a specified variable for zero? As I see, the algorithm could handle the zero itself.
In hash table, zero means empty. So, we need `hasZero` for hashed value 0.
I do not understand what does `(log2(rhsSize-1)) + 2` mean
In order to make 2^newSizeDegree is at least bigger than rhsSize.
Should we consider the `lhsSize` for `newSizeDegree`? As `max(max(rhsSize+2, lhsSize+2), uniquesHashSetInitialSizeDegree)`.
If `p.bufSize() >= uint32(rhsSize)`, there is no need to resize, the followed up process will insert element by `insertHash` and invoke `shrinkIfNeed`.
Why not add a check for `ast.AggFuncApproxCountDistinct` in NeedCount?
Because `AggFuncApproxCountDistinct` need tiflash to compute partial result and serialize it into string. This behavior is not like count.

Why this is checked here?

Should we return an error when rhsSize exceeding `uniquesHashMaxSize` and shrink can not be done anymore?

This check is to avoid corner case when engine return illegal partial result.
In fact, it should not happen.
Add a comment for why we need this?
What if `res` exceeds `p32`? It looks wired.

When res exceeds p32, fixedRes will become a very large number like 1.8 * 10^18.
This algorithm may lose accuracy when number of distinct element is more than 2^32.
Yeah, can we add a code comment for this phenomenon?
